domain_restrictions: F belongs to the polynomial ring over the integers.
The coefficients c_j are integers because F has integer coefficients.
The index j is always an integer.
In the symmetry assumption, j ranges from 0 to D inclusive.
In the first nonnegativity assumption, j ranges from 0 to floor of D divided by 2 inclusive.
The displayed expansion of F uses only coefficients c_0 through c_D.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: If the coefficients of a polynomial over the integers are symmetric around degree D and the coefficients in the first half are nonnegative, then every coefficient is nonnegative.
quantifier_order: Fix a polynomial F in the polynomial ring over the integers, with coefficients c_0 through c_D.
For every integer j between 0 and D inclusive, c_j equals c_{D minus j}.
For every integer j between 0 and floor of D divided by 2 inclusive, c_j is nonnegative.
Therefore, for every integer j between 0 and D inclusive, c_j is nonnegative.

variables.domain: integers indexed by j from 0 to D
variables.name: c_j

variables.domain: integers in the stated index ranges
variables.name: j

witness_dependencies: The coefficients c_j are determined by the chosen polynomial F and the displayed expansion up to degree D.

statement_nl: Let D be a nonnegative integer, and let F(q) = sum_{j=0}^D c_j q^j be a polynomial in Z[q]. Assume that c_j = c_{D-j} for every integer j with 0 <= j <= D, and assume also that c_j >= 0 for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2). Then c_j >= 0 for every integer j with 0 <= j <= D. Equivalently, every coefficient of F(q) is nonnegative.
